title_he: הָיִיתִי הֶחוֹטֵא הָאָשֵׁם, וַיְרַחֵם עָלַי יֵשׁוּעַ
review: The hymn is a converted sinner's testimony: 1:1–8 is 1 Tim 1:15 with Matt 9:12 and Luke 15:20, 2:1–8 is Mark 5:26 (the woman who spent all) with Jer 8:22, 3:1–8 is Ps 103:3 with Hos 6:1 and Mark 2:17, and 4:1–8 is Acts 4:12 with Matt 11:28 (nearly verbatim in the closing couplet).

4:7–8 quote the Lord's invitation, so the Hebrew uses the colon at 4:6 and lets the last two lines be His voice; the wording follows Matt 11:28's יְגֵעִים וּטְעוּנִים, because the stanza has been describing exactly that weariness.

2:6 וְהַיֵּאוּשׁ כְּנֶגְדִּי — the Arabic وَالْيَأْسُ كَالْمَرِيب is obscure ('despair like the suspect'); the Hebrew keeps the sense of despair standing opposite the soul without importing a figure the Arabic does not clearly make.
